    73	## 2. Behaviour
    74	
    75	The simulation engine ([mine/engine/](mine/engine/)) steps the whole mine five times a second. Each step
    76	covers 12 seconds of mine time, so mine time runs **60× faster than real time: one real minute is one mine
    77	hour**. The clock is published as `kpi.sim_time_h`. The engine publishes every state change to Ditto as
    78	Ditto-protocol `merge` commands over MQTT (about 28 commands per second in total).
    79	
    80	| Process | Model | Code |
    81	|---|---|---|
    82	| Truck travel | Rimpull/grade-resistance speed per road segment (drivetrain efficiency by drive type), speed caps (ramp, winter, visibility) | `models/truck.py` |
    83	| Haul cycle | Queue -> spot -> load (bucket passes × swing time) -> haul -> dump queue (2 bays) -> dump -> return; one truck at a time per shovel | `simulation.py` |
    84	| Loading | Swing time from fragmentation and cold-weather hydraulics | `models/shovel.py` |
    85	| Blasting | Kuz-Ram X50/X80 from powder factor | `models/blast.py` |
    86	| Crushing, grinding | Crusher capacity; SAG throughput from feed size, ore hardness (Axb) and available power, limited by the ball mills in service; Bond P80; mills draw their available power unless starved | `models/comminution.py`, `simulation.py` |
    87	| Flotation | Constant-tails recovery; grind (P80) and residence-time penalties | `models/flotation.py` |
    88	| Stockpiles | Mass and grade balance (well-mixed) for ROM, crushed, high-grade and waste piles; mass is conserved | `models/stockpile.py` |
    89	| Reliability | Weibull wear-out mode with a condition signal, plus random faults; all-causes MTBF from the reference table | `models/reliability.py` |
    90	| Dust | US EPA AP-42 unpaved-road PM10 on truck vehicle-km; watering only above 0 °C | `models/dust.py` |
    91	| Weather | Temperature, wind and visibility toward scenario targets | `models/weather.py` |
    92	| Economics, energy | Net smelter revenue, costs, diesel and grid energy, CO₂ | `models/economics.py`, `modules/energy.py` |
    93	
    94	#### Interlinked processes
    95	
    96	Trucks deliver ore to the ROM pad at the grade of the face they loaded. The crusher
    97	draws the ROM pad, plus high-grade ore when grade control asks for it, into the crushed-ore stockpile. The SAG
    98	mill draws that stockpile at a rate set by fragmentation, hardness, power and the ball mills in service.
    99	Flotation recovery then follows the feed grade and grind. Pit-side changes reach the plant only through the
   100	stockpiles. That is why haulage scenarios hit "ore mined" first and plant KPIs later.
   101	
   102	#### Back-pressure
   103	
   104	The coupling also runs from plant to pit:
   105	- the crusher stops when the crushed-ore stockpile is full;
   106	- ore trucks wait at the dump when the ROM pad (150 kt) is full.
   107	
   108	The engine checks that mass is conserved (`test_ore_mass_balance_closes`).
   109	
   110	#### Realistic constraints
   111	
   112	Examples:
   113	- one truck at a time under a shovel;
   114	- two dump bays;
   115	- winter speed caps;
   116	- no road watering below 0 °C;
   117	- crusher, mill and stockpile capacities;
   118	- one ball mill down cuts the grinding circuit to 60 % of its capacity;
   119	- fume re-entry times after blasting;
   120	- a closed ramp forces a 2.7 km detour;
   121	- with every shovel on a route down, trucks wait;
   122	- only the two electric-drive trucks can use a trolley line.
   123	
   124	#### Shadow baseline
   125	
   126	The engine runs a second simulation that never receives scenarios. Each time a scenario
   127	is applied or undone, the baseline restarts as an exact copy of the live mine at that moment, including
   128	stockpiles, equipment states and random-number streams. From then on the two differ only because of the
   129	scenario. Each machine also draws its failure times from its own random stream seeded by its name, so both
   130	runs see the same breakdowns. The `kpi` twin publishes `current_*`, `baseline_*` and `delta_*_pct` for
   131	16 KPIs (including grinding energy in kWh per tonne milled). Right after a click every delta is zero, and right after Undo they return to zero. Rate KPIs (ore mined,
   132	diesel, grid energy, haul cycle) are one-mine-hour moving averages, so they move over about a minute of real time.

   185	## 4. Modules
   186	
   187	Each module makes a decision on its own while the mine runs, and its result is written to twin features.
   188	
   189	### 4.1 Dispatch and grade control: the fleet-management system (Haulage and Dispatch; Geology and Ore Quality)
   190	
   191	#### Dispatch decision
   192	
   193	Whenever a truck finishes dumping, the dispatcher sends it to an eligible shovel:
   194	- the one with the shortest queue;
   195	- skipping broken, closed-off or fume-blocked shovels;
   196	- if every shovel on its route is down, the truck waits and asks again.
   197	
   198	Code: [mine/engine/modules/dispatch.py](mine/engine/modules/dispatch.py).
   199	
   200	#### Grade-control decision
   201	
   202	When the ROM pad grade falls below the 0.50 % Cu target, a loader reclaims the
   203	high-grade stockpile (0.65 % Cu) into the crusher feed. It runs in the proportion that restores the target, up
   204	to 800 t/h, and stops when the grade recovers.
   205	Code: [mine/engine/modules/grade_control.py](mine/engine/modules/grade_control.py).
   206	
   207	Without the system (`dispatch_policy: "fixed"`, the **Fleet-management system offline** scenario):
   208	- trucks keep their shift-plan shovels;
   209	- a truck whose shovel breaks waits 30 minutes for a supervisor to reassign it by radio ("reassigned by radio"
   210	  in the event log), and the new assignment holds until shift change;
   211	- grade control stops.
   212	
   213	#### Where it shows
   214	
   215	- each truck's `assigned_shovel` and shovel queue lengths;
   216	- "rerouted" lines in the event log when a shovel breaks;
   217	- `stockpile-hg.reclaim_tph` and `kpi.gc_reclaim_tph`;
   218	- the event lines "grade control: ... reclaiming" and "... stopped".
   219	
   220	#### Measured effect
   221	
   222	Shovel S2 failure, 12 mine hours, against the shadow baseline, mean of 8 seeded runs
   223	(`tools/validate.py`):
   224	
   225	| | Ore mined | Copper output, mine hours 2-12 |
   226	|---|---|---|
   227	| System on | −23 % | −2.8 % |
   228	| System offline (same failure, `dispatch_policy: "fixed"`) | −28 % | −6.6 % |
   229	
   230	The system saves about 5 points of ore and more than half of the copper loss. In normal running with balanced
   231	shovels its tonnage effect is about zero.
   232	
   233	### 4.2 Predictive maintenance (Equipment Maintenance and Reliability)
   234	- Decision. Every truck carries a coolant-temperature and oil-iron signal that rises as its wear-out
   235	  failure approaches. The engine estimates health and hours to wear-out from that signal; it does not see the
   236	  hidden failure time. With the strategy on (**Predictive maintenance** scenario), crossing the watch level
   237	  raises a work order, and the truck is repaired at the next shift change (5-7 h, no tow) instead of failing
   238	  in service (4-8 h plus a tow). Random faults stay unpredictable.
   239	- Where it shows.
   240	  - estimated `health_pct`, `coolant_temp_c` and `next_pm_due_h` on every truck;
   241	  - "predictive work order raised" and "planned repair" events;
   242	  - `kpi.current_unplanned_failures` against `kpi.baseline_unplanned_failures`, and `kpi.current_planned_repairs`.
   243	- Effect. It pays off over days of mine time. Over 200 mine hours (about 3.3 real hours), summed over 8 seeded
   244	  runs (`tools/validate.py`), unplanned failures fell 23 % (191 against 249, with 73 planned repairs instead), so
   245	  there are fewer in-service breakdowns and tows. Mean fleet availability stayed about the same (92.2 % against
   246	  92.2 %), because planned repairs also take trucks out. The literature reports +2 to +3 points (§8.2, §11-S9); the
   247	  twin's planned-repair time is conservative.
   248	- Code: [mine/engine/models/reliability.py](mine/engine/models/reliability.py), [mine/engine/modules/maintenance.py](mine/engine/modules/maintenance.py).
   249	
   250	### 4.3 Energy and CO₂ (Energy)
   251	- What it does. Accounting rather than a control decision:
   252	  - diesel by truck class and haul phase;
   253	  - grid power: crushing, conveying, grinding (mills draw their available power unless starved) and the trolley
   254	    line, whose draw follows the electric trucks under it;
   255	  - both converted into cost and CO₂ with Kazakh tariffs and a 0.80 kg CO₂/kWh grid factor.
   256	- Where it shows. `kpi.current_fuel_l_h`, `kpi.current_energy_kwh_h`, `kpi.current_co2_t_h` and their
   257	  baselines; `substation-01.load_kw`; mill `power_kw`.
   258	- Effect. **Enable trolley assist** puts the two Komatsu 830E trucks on the main ore ramp: fleet diesel

   261	  cuts grid energy and CO₂ 13-23 % together with output.
   262	- Code: [mine/engine/modules/energy.py](mine/engine/modules/energy.py).

   340	## Data and Assumptions
   341	
   342	#### Real versus synthetic
   343	
   344	- All telemetry is synthetic. It is generated by the simulation engine. No operational data from any
   345	  company is used.
   346	- The mine is fictional. "Kyzyl-Tas" and its layout are invented. Its parameters are taken from public
   347	  sources about Bozshakol and Aktogay, KAZ Minerals' operations in Kazakhstan.
   348	- No third-party datasets are stored in this repository.
   349	
   350	#### Where the parameters come from
   351	
   352	Every number in [mine/engine/models/constants.py](mine/engine/models/constants.py)
   353	carries a tag and a section reference into [mine/docs/03_domain.md](mine/docs/03_domain.md). That document lists
   354	each value with its source, equations and worked examples. Section 12 there has the full source list.
   355	
   356	| Tag | Meaning |
   357	|---|---|
   358	| [R] | Reported by the operator (KAZ Minerals reports and presentations) |
   359	| [V] | Vendor or OEM specification |
   360	| [L] | Literature, standards, regulators |
   361	| [D] | Derived from cited numbers; the calculation is shown |
   362	| [A] | Engineering assumption with a stated range (synthetic) |

   385	- the haul-road network and pit geometry;
   386	- maintenance and failure parameters, since no public site data exists;
   387	- the high-grade stockpile size (150 kt) and grade (0.65 % Cu);
   388	- the grade-control target (0.50 %) and loader rate (800 t/h);
   389	- the ROM pad capacity (150 kt) and the crushed-ore stockpile starting 70 % full;
   390	- the fixed plant (crusher, mills) starting early in its maintenance cycle, as after a scheduled reline;
   391	- the ball-mill design margin (20 % above nominal) and mill no-load power (25 %);
   392	- the 30-minute radio reassignment without a dispatch system;
   393	- the 0.80 kg CO₂/kWh grid factor, the central value of a 0.60-1.05 range;

   398	
   399	- Fleet size and strip ratio. The twin has 14 trucks, 10 on ore and 4 on waste, against Bozshakol's 18. It

   410	## 7. Limitations
   411	
   412	- Haul trips. Each haul leg is timed as one block over its road segments. Per-segment traffic counts are
   413	  therefore estimated from segment length, not from truck positions.
   414	- Not modelled:
   415	  - fuel tank levels and refuelling;
   416	  - block-model grade variability (each face has one grade);
   417	  - the slope-failure event itself (the slope alarm closes the ramp; the wall does not fail);
   418	  - drill availability feeding back into blasting.
   419	- Copper price drop. It changes revenue only; the cut-off grade does not move.
   420	- Scenario parameters. Wind, slope-radar velocity and fume-delay length exist only inside their preset
   421	  scenarios; the other drivers are adjustable through the custom what-if.
   422	- Back-pressure. Plant-to-pit back-pressure (ROM pad full) takes days of mine time to build up.

   424	  the chosen rock factor. Relative changes match.
   425	- Dispatch rule. Dispatch uses a shortest-queue rule, not a full LP optimiser.

     1	# Kyzyl-Tas - a digital twin of an open-pit copper mine on OpenEgiz
     2	
     3	Kyzyl-Tas is a fictional open-pit copper-gold mine with a 30 Mt/a concentrator. Its equipment, process
     4	capacities, grades and costs are taken from public data for Kazakhstan's Bozshakol and Aktogay operations
     5	(sources in [SUBMISSION.md](SUBMISSION.md#data-and-assumptions)). Every mine object is an Eclipse Ditto twin
     6	on the OpenEgiz platform. A physics-based simulation engine drives the twins over MQTT. A 3D web interface
     7	reads them back from the platform and runs what-if scenarios.

    12	from the repository root:
    13

    15	sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y make
    16	make up
    17	```

    19	`make up` starts the OpenEgiz platform and the mine together. The first run downloads about 2.5 GB of images
    20	and takes several minutes. When it finishes it prints the addresses below. No other step is needed.

    37	## A two-minute tour
    38	
    39	1. Open http://localhost:8000. Haul trucks move in the pit and the mine clock runs at 60× (one real minute is
    40	   one mine hour). The right panel shows live KPIs, each next to the value of a parallel baseline run.
    41	2. In **What-if scenarios**, click **Shovel S2 failure**. Within about a minute:
    42	   - shovel S2 turns red in the 3D view and on the minimap;
    43	   - its trucks are re-dispatched to S1 and the event log records the chain;
    44	   - ore mined and ore grade fall against the baseline;
    45	   - grade control starts reclaiming the high-grade stockpile (highlighted in 3D).
    46	3. Click **↺ Undo - back to baseline**. Every scenario field returns to its default, S2 returns to service and
    47	   the comparison restarts from zero.
    48	4. Open **Twin model** (top right of the 3D view) to browse all twins, or click any machine for its live data.
    49	   **Custom what-if** at the top of the scenario panel sets the scenario twin's values directly: shovel out,
    50	   trucks parked, crusher, powder factor, dispatch, temperature, ore hardness, mill power, road condition, copper price.

    57	mine-engine (Python simulation)
    58	   │  Ditto protocol "merge" commands, MQTT topic telemetry/<twin>
    59	   ▼
    60	Mosquitto ──► Eclipse Ditto (87 twins, namespace kz.kyzyltas.mine) ──► MQTT events ──► Telegraf ──► InfluxDB
    61	                 ▲                    │                                                              │

- A shovel taken down by a scenario returns to service at once, and a fume exclusion lifts.
- The shadow baseline restarts as a copy of the mine, so every delta returns to zero.
- Scenarios stay active until undone. A restarted engine reads the scenario twin and continues where it was.
